newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan and IMF agree on $1.6 bln loan.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan and IMF agree on $1.6 bln loan.

text.p: Pakistan and the International Monetary Fund said on Thursday they had agreed on a medium-term loan facility of at least $1.6 billion.

Fund director for the Middle East Paul Chabrier told a news conference that the loan would be a mix of an extended structural adjustment facility (ESAF) and extended fund facility, with ESAF forming the major part.
"Apart from very minor details, we have agreed on this programme and we will bring it back to Washington," he said.
Pakistan Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said: "I am glad to say that we have reached an agreement on the main elements of the policy framework paper."
Pakistan and IMF had been negotiating for a $1.2 billion to $1.5 billion, three-year loan for balance of payments support.
Charbier and his team will prepare the draft of a policy framework paper for consideration by the IMF executive board that will need to give the final approval for any loan.
